newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles city council holds airport funds.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles city council holds airport funds.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council voted on Tuesday not to return $31 million to the Los Angeles International Airport in a move that could provoke the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), city officials said.

The city council voted to hold onto the funds and to proceed, if necessary, to an administrative hearing to settle the dispute. The council plans to keep the disputed funds in a city trust account until the issue is resolved, according to a spokesman for the city's controller.

Los Angeles City Controller Rick Tuttle maintained that the $31 million was repayment for past investments by the city in the airport. The investments were for fire safety and certain public works projects.
The FAA contended that airport debt was settled and gave officials until December 2 to give back the money.
City Councilman Nate Holden warned that Tuesday's vote could spark a legal battle between the FAA and the council.
"It's back in the FAA's court," Holden said after the council meeting. "If they (the FAA) sue, they're going to win. I don't think the city has a legal leg to stand on."
In October, Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., charged that Los Angeles improperly diverted the funds and threatened to push to have the city's federal airport funding slashed by that amount.
